subject: QC gate coverage gap (Nancy, 2026-07-30): qc-hexgrad.sh extracts and runs the Python VERIFY block only -- it never exercises accumulates()/builtRealEngine(), which are JS living in the challenge tests[] arrays. So a future edit could reintroduce a regex regression (exactly the false-negative that blocked honest learners) and the gate would still report PASSED. Add a node-based check of the tests[] functions to qc-lab tooling. Applies to every future Model Forge gate, not just HexGrad.
description: [2026-08-01 16:07] DONE (committed, not deployed -- tooling only). qc-js-checks.js EXTRACTS accumulates()/builtRealEngine() from the lab page and evaluates them; 13 cases, weighted toward honest spellings because the historical failure was a FALSE NEGATIVE that blocked a correct engine scoring GRADCHECK 6/6. MUTATION-TESTED: reverting accumulates() to the +=-only version makes the gate exit 1 with exactly the 2 non-+= spellings failing; shipped page exits 0. Wired as step [3/3] of qc-hexgrad.sh. #257's known-open case (self.grad = other.grad + 0) is printed every run by its exact input and deliberately NOT counted as a failure.
